name: weighted opportunity rating mean per game averages the PER-GAME combine (executed-result parity)
description: The deliverable of the combined-measure period CTE, as a number. WOPR has no single measure_expr, so its per-period value exists only once the combine is evaluated at PERIOD grain over each accumulator's per-game sum -- and a mean over that is not the pooled combine. The seed makes those two answers DIFFERENT so the fixture can tell them apart: two receivers over two games, with game 1 carrying 5 team targets and 50 team air yards (A takes 1 target and 30 air yards, B takes 4 and 20) and game 2 carrying 4 and 40 (A takes 3 and 10, B takes 1 and 30). Per game A is 1.5*(1/5)+0.7*(30/50)=0.72 then 1.5*(3/4)+0.7*(10/40)=1.30, so the mean is 1.01; B is 1.48 then 0.90, so 1.19. Pooling instead gives 0.9778 and 1.2222 -- so an emitter that projected the pooled value and averaged one row per subject fails this. The shares are also asymmetric about one half, so transposing the 1.5 and the 0.7 weights yields {0.97, 1.23} rather than a permutation of {1.01, 1.19}; the harness compares order-insensitively, and a symmetric seed would stay green under exactly that transposition.
